title: The Castle of Perseverance
author: Anonymous (Middle English)
note: Middle English text of the play as edited by F. J. Furnivall and A. W. Pollard in The Macro Plays, Early English Text Society, Extra Series 91 (London, 1904), from the Macro manuscript. The banns and the whole play are given, with the speakers' names and stage directions as printed; Pollard's introduction, the stage plan, the side-notes, footnotes, marginal glosses and glossary are omitted, as are the line numbers, Furnivall's scene numbers and the editors' scripture references. Thorn and yogh are kept. The sections follow Furnivall's scenes, Scene VI being divided into parts for length. Square brackets are the editors' own marks for letters or words supplied. Two leaves of the manuscript are lost, so the text has a gap after line 1603 and another near the end of Scene VII. Transcribed from scanned pages.
blurb: Mankind (Humanum Genus) is born between a Good and a Bad Angel and chooses the World. He is led through the Seven Deadly Sins by Pride, Wrath, Envy, Gluttony, Sloth and Lechery, and finally by Covetousness. The Virtues, led by Meekness, shelter him in a castle, and Covetousness at last lures him out of it. Old Mankind dies, and his Soul is dragged towards hell until the four daughters of God (Mercy, Peace, Righteousness and Truth) plead for him before the throne.

sections.title: The Banns
sections.text:
Primus Vexil[lator]. Glorious God! in all degres, lord most of myth,
þat heuene & erthe made of nowth, boþe se & londe,
þe aunȝelys in heuene, hym to serue bryth,
& [man]-kynde in mydylerd he made with hys honde,
& [our lo]fly lady, þat lanterne is of lyth,
Save oure lege lord, þe kynge, þe leder of þis londe,
& all þe ryallis of þis revme, & rede hem þe ryth,
& all þe goode comowns of þis towne þat be-forn us stonde
In þis place!
We mustyr ȝou with menschepe,
& Freyne ȝou of Frely frenchepe,
Cryst safe ȝou all fro schenchepe,
þat knowyn wyl oure case!

Secundus Vexillator. þe case of oure comynge, ȝou to declare,
euery man in hym self, for sothe he it may fynde.
whon mankynde in-to þis werld born is ful bare,
& bare schal beryed be at [t]he [l]ast ende,
God hym ȝeuyth to aungelis Ful ȝep & ful ȝare,
þe goode aungel & þe badde, to hym for to lende:
þe goode techyth hym goodnesse; þe badde, synne & sare;
Whanne þe ton hath þe victory, þe toþer goth be-hende,
be skyll.
þe goode aungel coueytyth euermore mans saluacion,
& þe badde bysytyth hem euere to hys dampnacion;
& God hathe govyn man fre arbritracion
Wheþer he wyl hymse[lf] saue or his soule per[yll.]
Primus Vexillator. spylt is man spetously, whanne he to synne asent;
þe bad aungel þanne bryngyth hym iij enmys so stout:
þe Werlde, þe Fende, þe foul Flesch so joly & jent;
þei ledyn hym Ful lustyly with synnys al a-bowt,
Pyth with Pride & Coueytyse, to þe werld is he went,
to meynten his manhod; all men to hym lout.
aftyre Ire & Envye, þe Fend hath to hym lent
Bakbytynge & endytynge, with all men for to route,
Ful evyn;
but þe fowle Flesch, homlyest of all,
Slawth, Lust & Leccherye, gun to hym call
Glotony, & oþer synnys, boþe grette & small:
þis mans soule is soylyd with synnys moo þanne seuyn.

Secundus Vexillator. whanne mans sowle is soylyd with synne & with sore,
þanne þe goode aungyl makyth mykyl mornynge
þat þe lofly lyknesse of God schulde be lore
þorwe þe badde aungellis fals entysynge.
He sendyth to hym concyens, pryckyd Ful pore,
& clere confescyon, with penauns doynge:
þei mevyn man to mendement þat he mys-dyd be-fore;
þus þei callyn hym to clennesse & to good levynge,
with-outyn dystaunce.
Mekenesse, Pacyense, & Charyte,
Sobyrnesse, Besynesse, & Chastyte,
& Largyte, uertuys of good degre,
Man callyth to þe Castel of good Perseueraunce.

Primus Vexillator. þe Castel of Perseuerans, wanne Mankynde hath tan,
Wel armyd with vertus, & ouercome alle vycys,
þere þe Good Aungyl makyth ful mery þanne
þat Mankynde hath ouercome his gostly e[n]mijs.
þe Badde Aungyl mornyþ þat he hath myssyd man;
He callyth þe Werld, þe Fende, & þe foule Flesch, I-wys,
& all þe seuene synnys to do þat þey canne
to brynge Mankynde a-geyn to bale out of blys,
With wronge.
Pride a-saylyth Meknesse with all his myth;
Ire, a-geyns Paciensse, ful fast ganne he fyth;
Envye, a-geyn Charyte strywyth ful ryth;
but Coveytyse a-geyns Largyte fytyth over longe.

ijus Vexillator. Coveytyse, Mankynde euere coveytyth for to qwell:
he gaderith to hym Glotony, a-ȝeyns Sobyrnesse;
Leccherye, with Chastyte ffytith ful fell,
& Slawthe in Goddis seruyse, a-geyns Besynesse.
þus vycys, a-geyns vertues fytyn ful snelle;
euery buskith to brynge man to dystresse;
but Penaunce & Confescion, with Mankynde wyl melle;
þe vycys arn ful lyckely, þe vertues to opresse:
sann dowte;
þus in þe Castel of good Perseuerance
Mankynde is maskeryd with mekyl varyaunce;
þe Goode Aungyl & þe Badde be euere at dystaunce;
þe Goode holdith hym Inne; þe Badde wolde brynge
hym owte.

jus Vexillator. Owt of good perseueraunce, whanne Mankynde wyl not come,
ȝyt þe Badde Aungyl, with Coveytyse hym gan a-sayle,
fyndende hym in pouerte & penaunce so be-nome,
& bryngyth hym in beleue, in defaute for to fayle,
þanne he profyrth hym good & gold, so gret a sowme,
þat if he wyl com a-geyn, & with þe world dayle,
þe Badde Aungyl to þe Werld tollyth hym downe,
þe Castel of Perseueraunce to Fle fro þe dayle
& blysse.
þanne þe Werld be-gynnyth hym to restore;
haue he neuere so mykyl, ȝyt he wold haue more:
þus þe badde aungyl leryth hym hys lore:
þe more a man agyth, þe harder he is.

Primus Vexillator. Hard a man is in age, & Covetouse be kynde;
Whanne all oþer synnys man hath for-sake,
Euere þe more þat he hath, þe more is in his mynde
to gader & to gete good with woo & with wrake:
þus þe Good Aungyl caste is be-hynde,
& þe Badde Aungyl, man to hym takyth,
þat wryngyth hym wrenchys to his last ende,
tyl Deth comyth foul dolfully, & loggyth hym in a lake ful lowe.
þanne is man on molde maskeryd in mynde;
he sendith afftyr his sekkatours, ful fekyl to fynde;
& his eyr aftyrward comyth euere be-hynde:
I wot not who is his name, for he hym nowt knowe.

Secundus Vexillator. Man knowe not who schal be his eyr,
& gouerne his good;
he caryth more for his catel þanne for his cursyd synne;
to putte his good in gouernaunce, he mengyth his mod;
he wolde þat it were scyfftyd a-mongis his ny kynne;
but þer schal com a lythyr ladde with a torne hod,—
I wot neuere who schal be his name, his clopis be ful þynne,—
schal eryth þe erytage þat neuere was of hys blod,
whanne al his lyfe is lytyd up-on a lytyl pynne,
at þe laste,
On lyue whanne [he] may no lenger lende,
Mercy he callyth at hys laste ende:
"Mercy, God! be now myn frende!"
with þat, mans spyryt is paste.

Primus Vexillator. whanne manis spyryt is past, þe Badde Aungyl ful fell
cleymyth þat, for couetyse, mans sowle schuld ben hys,
& for to bere it ful boystowsly with hym in-to hell.
þe Good Aungyl seyth "nay! þe spyryt schal to blys,
For, at his laste ende, of mercy he gan spell,
& þerfore, of mercy schal he nowth mysse;
& oure lofly lady, if sche wyl for hym mell,
be mercy & be menys, in purgatory he is,
in Ful bytter place.
þus mowthys confession
& his hertys contricion
schal saue man fro dampnacion,
be Goddys mercy & grace.

Secundus Vexillator. Grace, if God wyl graunte us, of hys mykyl myth,
þese parcellis in propyrtes we purpose us to playe
þis day seuenenyt, be-fore ȝou in syth,
At [ ] on þe grene, in ryall a-ray.
ȝe haste ȝou þanne þedyrward, syris, hendly in hyth,
All goode neyboris, ful specyaly we ȝou pray,
& loke þat ȝe be þere be-tyme, luffely & lyth,
for we schul be onward be vnderne of þe day.
dere Frendys,
we thanke ȝou of all good dalyaunce
& of all ȝoure specyal sportaunce,
& preye ȝou of good contynnaunce
to oure lyuys endys.

Primus Vexillator. Deus, oure lyuys we loue ȝou, þus takande oure leue.
ȝe manly men of [ ], þus Crist saue ȝou all!
he maynten ȝoure myrthis, & kepe ȝou fro greve,
þat born was of Mary myld in an ox stall.
Now, mercy be all [ ], & wel mote ȝe cheve!
All oure feythful frendys, þus fayre mote ȝe fall!
ȝa, & welcum be ȝe whanne ȝe com, prys for to preve,
& worthyi to be worchepyd in boure, & in hall,
& in euery place.
fare-wel, fayre frendys,
þat lofly wyl lystyn & lendis!
Cryste kepe ȝou fro fendis!
trumpe up, & lete vs pace!

sections.title: Scene I: Before the Scaffold of Mundus
sections.text:
Mundus. Worthy wytis, in al þis werd wyde,
Be wylde wode wonys, & euery weye-went,
Precyous in prise, prekyd in pride,
þorwe þis propyr pleyn place, in pes be ȝe bent!
Buske ȝou, bolde bacheleris, vnder my baner to a-byde,
Where bryth basnetis be bateryd, & backys ar schent,
ȝe, syrys semly, all same syttyth on syde,
For, bothe be see & be londe, my sondis I haue sent;
al þe werld myn nam[e] is ment,
al a-bowtyn my bane is blowe,
In euery cost I am knowe,
I do men rawyn on ryche rowe
tyl þei be dyth to dethys dent.

Assarye, Acaye, & Almayne,
Canadoyse, Capadoyse & Cananee,
Babyloyne, Brabon, Burgoyne, & Bretayne,
Grece, Galys, & to þe Gryckysch see;
I meue also Masadoyne in my mykyl mayne,
Fraunc, Flaundrys, & Freslonde, & also Normande,
Pyncecras, Parys, & longe Pygmayne,
& euery toun in Trage, euyn to þe dreye tre,
Rodis & ryche Rome,
all þese londis, at myn a-vyse,
arn castyn to my werdly wyse;
My tresorer, Syr Coueytyse,
hath sesyd hem holy to me.

þerfor my game & my gle growe ful glad;
þer is wythe in þis werld, þat my wytte wyl me werne,
Euery ryche rengne rapyth hym ful rad,
In lustis & in lykyngis my lawys to lerne;
With fayre folke, in þe felde, freschly I am fadde;
I dawnse doun, as a doo, be dalys ful derne:
What boy bedyth batayl, or debatyth with blad,
hym were betyr to ben hangyn hye in hell herne,
or brent on lyth leuene.
Who-so spekyth a-ȝeyn þe werd,
In a presun he schal be sperd;
myn hest is holdyn, & herd
In-to hyȝe heuene. [Exit.]

sections.title: Scene II: Before Belial's Scaffold
Scene III: Before the Scaffold of Caro
Scene IV: On the Castle-Green
sections.text:
(Enter Mankind, with a Good Angel on his right, and a Bad Angel on his left.)

Humanum Genus. aftyr oure forme faderis kende,
þis nyth I was of my moder born.
Fro my moder I walke, I wende;
Ful feynt & febyl, I fare ȝou be-forn;
I am nakyd of lym & lende,
as mankynde is schapyn & schorn;
I not wedyr to gon ne to lende,
to helpe my-self mydday nyn morn:
for schame I stonde & schende.
I was born þis nyth in blody ble,
& nakyd I am, as ȝe may se.
a! Lord God in trinite!
Whow Mankende is vnthende!

Where-to I was to þis werld browth,
I ne wot; but to woo & wepynge
I am born, & haue ryth nowth
to helpe my self in no doynge.
I stonde & stodye, al ful of þowth;
bare & pore is my clothynge;
a sely crysme, myn hed hath cawth,
þat I tok at myn crystenynge:
certis, I haue no more.
of erthe I cam, I wot ryth wele;
&, as erthe, I stande þis sele;
of mankende it is gret dele.
Lord God, I crye þyne ore!

ij aungels bene a-synyd to me;
þe ton techyth me to goode:
on my ryth syde ȝe may hym se;
he cam fro Criste þat deyed on rode.
a-noþer is ordeynyd her to be,
þat is my foo, be fen & flode;
he is a-bout, in euery degre,
to drawe me to þo dewylys wode,
þat in helle ben thycke.
swyche to, hath euery man on lyue,
to rewlyn hym & hys wyttis fyue:
whanne man doth ewyl, þe ton wolde schryue;
þe tother drawyth to wycke.

but syn þese aungelys be to me falle,
Lord Jhesu! to ȝou I bydde a bone,
þat I may folwe, be strete & stalle,
þe aungyl þat cam fro heuene trone.
now, Lord Jhesu! in heuene halle,
here, whane I make my mone!
Coryows Criste, to ȝou I calle;
as a grysly gost, I grucche & grone,
I wene, ryth ful of thowth.
a! Lord Jhesu! wedyr may I goo?
a crysyme I haue, & no moo.
alas! men may be wondyr woo
Whanne þei be fyrst forth browth.

Bonus Angelus. ȝa, forsothe; & þat is wel sene:
of woful wo, man may synge,
for iche creature helpith hym-self be-dene,
Saue only man at hys comynge.
neuyr-þe-lesse, turne þee fro tene,
& serue Jhesu, heuene kynge,
& þou schalt, be greuys grene,
fare wel in alle thynge
þat Lord þi lyfe hath lante.
haue hym alway in þi mynde,
þat deyed on rode for mankynde,
& serue hym to þi lyfes ende,
& sertis þou schalt not wante!

Malus Angelus. Pes, aungel! þi wordis are not wyse!
þou counselyst hym not a-ryth;
he schal hym drawyn to þe werldis seruyse,
to dwelle with caysere, kynge, & knyth,
þat in londe be hym non lyche.
Cum on with me, stylle as ston!
þou & I, to þe werd schul goon,
& þanne þou schalt sen a-non
whow sone þou schalt be ryche.

Bonus Angelus. A, pes, aungel! þou spekyst folye!
Why schuld he coueyt werldis goode,
syn Criste in erthe, & hys meynye,
all in pouert here þei stode?
werldis wele, be strete & stye,
Faylyth & fadyth, as fysch in flode;
but he[ue]ne-ryche is good & trye,
þer Criste syttyht, bryth as blode,
With-outyn any dystresse.
to þe world, wolde he not flyt,
but forsok it euery whytt:
example I fynde in holy wryt,
he wyl bere me wytnesse:
diuicias & paupertates ne dederis mihi, Domine.

Malus Angelus. ȝa, ȝa, man! leue hym nowth,
but cum with me, be stye & strete!
haue þou a gobet of þe werld cawth,
þou schalt fynde it good & swete.
a fayre lady, þee schal be tawth,
þat in bowre þi bale schal bete;
with ryche rentis þou schalt be frawth;
with sylke sendel to syttyn in sete.
I rede, late Bedys be!
If þou wylt haue wel þyn hele,
& faryn wel at mete & mele,
with Goddis seruyse may þou not dele,
but cum & folwe me.

Humanum Genus. Whom to folwe, wetyn I ne may:
I stonde in stodye, & gynne to raue;
I wolde be ryche in gret a-ray,
& fayn I wolde my sowle saue:
as wynde in watyr I wave. [To the Bad Angel.]
þou woldyst, to þe werld I me toke;
& he wolde þat I it for-soke.
now, so God me helpe, & þe holy boke,
I not wyche I may haue.

Malus Angelus. Cum on, man! where-of hast þou care?
go we to þe werld, I rede þee blyue;
for þer þou schalt mow ryth wel fare,
In case if þou þynke for to thryue;
no lord schal be þee lyche.
take þe werld to þine entent,
& late þi loue be þer-on lent;
With gold & syluyr, & ryche rent,
a-none þou schalt be ryche.

Humanum Genus. now, syn þou hast be-hetyn me so,
I wyl go with þee & a-say;
I ne lette, for frende i.e fo,
but with þe Werld I wyl go play,
certis, a lytyl þrowe.
In þis World is al my trust,
to lyuyn in lykyng & in lust:
haue he & I onys cust,
we schal not part, I trowe.

Bonus Angelus. a! nay! man! for Cristis blod,
cum a-gayn be strete & style!
þe Werld is wyckyd, & ful wod,
& þou schalt leuyn but a whyle.
What coueytyst þou to wynne?
man! þynke on þyn endynge day
Whanne þou schalt be closyd vnder clay!
& if þou thenke of þat a-ray,
certis þou schalt not synne.
homo, memento finis! & in eternum non peccabis.

Malus Angelus. ȝa, on þi sowle þou schalt þynke al be tyme.
Cum forth, man, & take non hede!
Cum on, & þou schalt holdyn hym Inne;
þi flesch þou schalt foster & fede
with lofly lyuys fode.
With þe World þou mayst be bold
tyl þou be sexty wynter hold.
wanne þi nose waxit cold,
þanne mayst þou drawe to goode.
Humanum Genus. I vow to God, & so I may
Make mery a ful gret throwe;
I may leuyn many a day;
I am but ȝonge, as I trowe,
for to do þat I schulde.
Myth I ryde be sompe & syke,
& be ryche, & lord [i-]lyke,
certis þanne schulde I be Fryke,
& a mery man on molde.

Malus Angelus. ȝys, be my feyth, þou schalt be a lord,
& ellys hange me be þe hals!
but þou muste be at myn a-cord;
oþer whyle þou muste be fals
a-monge kythe & kynne.
Now go we forth, swythe a-non!
to þe Werld us must gon;
& bere þee manly euere a-mong,
Whanne þou comyst out or Inne.

Humanum Genus. ȝys, & ellys haue þou my necke.
but I be manly be downe & dyche;
& þou I be fals, I ne recke,
with so þat I be lord [i-]lyche,
I folwe þee as I can.
þou schalt be my bote of bale;
for, were I ryche of holt & hale,
þanne wolde I ȝeue neuere tale
of God ne of good man. [Exeunt Mal. Ang. and Hum. Gen.]

Bonus Angelus. I weyle, & wrynge & make mone!
þis man, with woo schal be pylt.
I sye sore, & grysly grone,
for hys folye schal make hym spylt;
I not weder to gone.
Mankynde hath forsakyn me!
alas, man, for loue of the!
ȝa, for þis gamyn & þis gle,
þou schalt grocchyn & grone. [Exit.] [pipe vp, mu[sic].]

sections.title: Scene V: Before World's Scaffold
sections.text:
(On the Scaffold, World, Pleasure, Liking, Vain-Glory.)

Mundus. Now I sytte in my semly sale;
I trotte & tremle in my trew trone;
as a hawke, I hoppe in my hende hale;
Kyng, knyth & kayser, to me makyn mone.
of God ne of good man, ȝyf I neuere tale;
as a lykynge lord, I leyke here a-lone;
wo-so brawle any boste, be downe or be dale,
þo gadlyngis schal be gastyd, & gryslych grone,
I-wys.
Lust, Foly & Veynglory,
all þese arn in myn memory:
þer be-gynnyth þe nobyl story
of þis werldis blys.

Lust, Lykyng & Foly,
comly knytis of renoun,
be-lyue þorwe þis londe do crye
al a-bowtyn in toure & toun.
If any man be fer or nye,
þat to my seruyse wyl buske hym boun,
if he wyl be trost & trye,
he schal be kyng, & were þe croun,
With rycches[t] robys in res.
wo-so to þe Werld wyl drawe,
Of God ne of good man ȝeuyt he not a hawe:
Syche a man, be londys lawe,
schal syttyn on my dees.

Voluptas. lo, me, here! redy, lord, to faryn & to fle,
to sekyn þee a seruaunt dynge & dere.
Who-so wyl with foly rewlyd be,
he is worthy to be a seruaunt here,
þat drawyth to synnys seuene.
Who-so wyl be fals & covetouse,
With þis werld he schal haue lond & house;
þis werldys wysdom ȝeuyth no[t] a louse
of God, nyn of hye heuene.
[tunc descendat in placea parita.]

Pes, pepyl! of pes we ȝou pray.
syth & sethe wel to my sawe!
Who-so wyl be ryche & in gret aray,
to-ward þe werld he schal drawe.
Who-so wyl be fals, al þat he may,
of God hym-self he hath non awe,
& lyuyn in lustis, nyth & day,
þe werld of hym wyl be ryth fawe,
do dwelle in his howse.
who-so wyl with þe werld haue his dwellynge,
& ben a lord of his clothynge,
he muste nedys, ouyr al þynge,
euere-more be couetowse:
Non est in mundo diues, qui dicit 'habundo.'

Stulticia. ȝa! couetouse he muste be,
& me, Foly, must haue in mende;
for who-so wyl alwey foly fle,
In þis werld schal ben vnthende.
þorwe werldys wysdom of gret degre,
Schal neuere man in werld moun wende,
but he haue help of me
þat am Foly fer & hende;
he muste hangyn on my hoke.
werldly wyt was neuere nout,
but with foly it were frawt;
þus þe wysman hath tawt
a-botyn in his boke:
Sapiencia penes Domini.
Voluptas. Now, all þe men þat in þis werld wold thryue,
for to rydyn on hors ful hye,
cum speke with Lust & Lykynge belyue,
& his felaw, ȝonge Foly!
late se who-so wyl vs knowe.
Who-so wyl drawe to Lykynge & Luste,
& as a fole, in foly ruste,
On vs to he may truste,
& leuyn louely, I trowe.

Malus Angelus (re-entering). How, Lust, Lykyng, & Folye!
take to me good entent!
I haue browth, be downys drye,
to þe Werld a gret present;
I haue gylyd hym ful qweyntly,
For, syn he was born, I haue hym blent;
he schal be serwaunt good & try;
a-monge ȝou his wyl is lent,
to þe Werld he wyl hym take;
For, syn he cowde wyt, I vndirstonde,
I haue hym tysyd in euery londe.
hys Goode Aungel, be strete & st[r]onde,
I haue don hym forsake.

þerfor, Lust, my trewe fere,
þou art redy al-wey I-wys;
of worldly lawys þou hym lere,
þat he were browth in werldly blys;
Loke he be ryche, þe soþe to tell;
help hym, fast he gunne to thrywe;
& whanne he wenyth best to lywe,
þanne schal he deye, & not be schrywe,
& goo with vs to hell.

Voluptas. be Satan, þou art a nobyl knawe
to techyn men fyrst fro goode!
Lust & Lykynge he schal haue;
Lechery schal ben hys fode;
Metis & drynkis he schal haue trye.
With a lykynge lady of lofte,
he schal syttyn in sendel softe,
to cachen hym to helle crofte
þat day þat he schal deye.

Stulticia. With ryche rentys I schal hym blynde,
Wyth þe werld tyl he be pytte;
& þanne schal I, longe or his ende,
make þat caytyfe to be knytte
On þe werld whanne he is set s[ore]. [Re-enter Mankind.]
Cum on, man! þou schalt not rewe,
for þou wylt be to vs trewe;
þou schalt be clad in clothis newe,
& be ryche euere-more.

Humanum Genus. Mary, felaw, gramercy!
I wolde be ryche & of gret renoun.
[Of God] I ȝeue no tale trewly,
So þat I be lord of toure & toun,
be buskys & bankys broun.
Syn þat þou wylt make me
boþe ryche of gold & fee,
goo forthe! for I wyl folow þee
be dale & euery towne.

[Trumpe vp. tunc ibunt Voluptas & Stulticia, Malus Angelus & Humanum Genus, ad Mundum, & dicat

Voluptas. How, lord! loke owt! for we haue browth
a serwant of nobyl fame; [Presents Mankind.]
of worldly good is al his þouth;
of lust & folye he hath no schame;
he wolde be gret of name,
he wolde be at gret honour,
for to rewle town & toure;
he wolde haue to his paramoure
Sum louely dynge dame.

Mundus [to Mankind]. welcum, syr, semly in syth!
þou art welcum to worthy wede,
for þou wylt be my seruaunt, day & nyth.
With my seruyse I schal þee foster & fede;
þi bak schal be betyn with besawntis bryth;
þou schalt haue byggyngys be bankis brede;
to þi cors schal knele kayser & knyth,
& ladys louely on lere,
Where þat þou walke, be sty or be strete.
but Goddys seruyse þou must forsake,
& holy to þe werld þee take,
& þanne a man I schal þee make,
þat non schal be þi pere.

Humanum Genus. ȝys, Werld, & þer-to here myn honde,
to forsake God & hys seruyse.
to medys, þou ȝeue me howse & londe,
þat I regne rychely at myn enprise
so þat I fare wel be strete & stronde
Whil I dwelle here in werldly wyse,
I reeke neuere of heuene wonde,
nor of Jhesu, þat jentyl justyse;
of my sowle I haue non rewthe.
what schulde I reckenen of domysday,
so þat I be ryche & of gret a-ray?
I schal make mery whyl I may,
& þer-to here my trewthe.

Mundus. Now sertis, syr, þou seyst wel:
I holde þee trewe ffro top to þe too.
but þou were ryche, it were gret del,
& all men þat wyl fare soo.
cum up, my serwaunt trew as stel! [tunc ascendit Humanum Genus ad Mundum.
þou schalt be ryche, where so þou goo;
men schul seruyn þee at mel
with mynstralsye & bemys blo,
with metis & drynkis trye.
lust & lykynge schal be þin ese;
louely ladys þee schal plese:
who-so do þee any disesse,
he schal ben hangyn hye.

Lykynge! be-lyue
late clothe hym swythe
In robys ryve
With ryche a-ray.
Folye! þou fonde,
be strete & stronde,
serue hym at honde
bothe nyth & day.

Voluptas. trostyly,
lord, redy,
Je vous pry,
Syr, I say.
in lyckynge & lust
he schal rust,
tyl dethys dust
do hym to day.

Stulti[cia]. & I, Folye,
schal hyen hym hye,
tyl sum enmye
hym ouer-goo.
In worldis wyt
þat in folye syt,
I þynke ȝyt
his sowle to sloo. [trumpe vp! [Exeunt.]

sections.title: Scene VI: The Seven Deadly Sins and the Castle (part 1 of 6)
sections.text:
[Enter Backbiter.]

Detraccio. all þyngis I crye a-gayn þe pes
to knyt & knaue; þis is my kende.
ȝa! dyngne dukis on her des,
In bytter balys I hem bynde;
cryinge & care, chydynge & ches
& sad sorwe, to hem I sende.
ȝa! lowde lesyngis lachyd in les,
of talys vn-trewe is al my mende;
Mannys bane a-bowtyn I bere.
I wyl þat ȝe wetyn, all þo þat ben here,
for I am knowyn, fer & nere,
I am þe werldys messengere;
my name is Bacbytere.

with euery wyth I walke & wende,
& euery man now louyth me wele;
with lowde lesyngis vndyr lende,
to dethys dynt I dresse & dele.
to speke fayre be-forn, & fowle be-hynde,
a-mongis men at mete & mele,
trewly, lordys, þis is my kynde.
þer I renne up-on a whele
I am feller þanne a fox.
fleterynge & flaterynge is my lessun;
with lesyngis I tene boþe tour & town,
with letterys of defamacyoun
I bere here in my box.

I am lyth of lopys þorwe euery londe;
myn holy happys may not ben hyd;
to may not to-gedyr stonde,
but I, Bakbyter, be þe thyrde.
I schape ȝone boyis to schame & schonde,
all þat wyl bowyn whanne I hem bydde;
to lawe of londe in feyth I fonde;
Whanne talys vntrewe arn be-tydde,
Bakbyter is wyde spronge:
þorwe þe werld, be downe & dalys,
all a-bowtyn I brewe balys;
Euery man tellyth talys
Aftyr my fals tunge.

þer-fore I am mad massenger
to lepyn ouer londis leye,
þorwe all þe world, fer & ner,
vnsayd sawys for to seye.
In þis holte I hunte here
for to spye a preuy pley;
For whanne Mankynde is cloþyd clere,
þanne schal I techyn hym þe wey
to þe dedly synnys seuene.
Here I schal a-bydyn with my pese,
þe wronge to do hym for to chese,
for I þynke þat he schal lese
þe lyth of hey heuene.

Voluptas [re-entering with the World, Mankind, and Folly]. Worthy World, in welthys wonde,
here is Mankynde ful fare in folde!
In bryth besauntys he is bownde,
& bon to bowe to ȝou so bolde.
he leuyth in lustys euery stounde;
holy to ȝou he hathe hym ȝolde.
for to makyn hym gay on grounde,
worthy World, þou art be-holde;
þis werld is wel at ese;
For to God I make a-vow,
Mankynde had leuer now
greue God with synnys row,
þanne þe World to dysplese.

Stulticia. dysplese þee, he wyl for no man;
On me, Folye, is al hys þowth.
trewly Mankynde nowth nen can
þynke on God þat hathe hym bowth.
worthy World, wyth as swan,
In þi loue lely is he lawth;
sythyn he cowde, & fyrste be-gan.
þee forsakyn wolde he nowth,
but ȝeue hym to folye;
& syþyn he hathe to þee be trewe,
I rede þee forsakyn hym for no newe;
lete vs plesyn hym tyl þat he rewe,
In hell to hangyn hye.

Mundus. now, Folye, fayre þee be-fall!
& Luste, blyssyd be þou ay!
ȝe han browth Mankynde to myn hall,
Sertis in a nobyl a-ray.
with werldys welthys, with-Inne þese wall,
I schal hym feffe of þat I may.
welcum Mankynde! to þee I call,
clenner cloþyd þanne any clay,
be downe, dale, & dyche.
Mankynde! I rede þat þou reste
with me, þe Werld, as it is beste;
loke þou holde myn hende feste,
& euere þou schalt be ryche.

Humanum Genus. Whou schul I, but I þi hestis helde?
þou werkyst with me holy my wyll;
þou feffyst me with fen & felde,
& hye hall, be holtis & hyll.
In werldly wele my wytte I welde;
In joye I jette, with juelys jentyll;
on blysful banke my boure is bylde,
In veynglorye I stonde styll;
I am kene as a knyt.
Who-so a-geyn þe werld wyl speke,
Mankynde schal on hym be wreke;
In stronge presun I schal hym steke,
be it wronge or ryth.

Mundus. a! Mankynde! wel þee be-tyde,
þat þi loue on me is sette!
In my bowris þou schalt a-byde,
& ȝyt fare makyl þe bette.
I Feffe þee in all my wonys wyde
In dale of dros, tyl þou be deth;
I make þee lord of mekyl pryde:
syr, at þyn owyn mowthis mette,
I fynde in þee no tresun.
In all þis worlde, be se & sonde,
parkis, placis, lawnde & londe,
here I ȝyfe þee with myn honde,
syr, an opyn sesun.

go to my tresorer, Syr Couetouse!
loke þou tell hym as I seye!
bydde hym make þee mayster in his house,
with penys & powndis for to pleye.
loke þou ȝeue not a lous
of þe day þat þou schalt deye.
messenger, do now þyne vse!
Bakbytere, teche hym þe weye!
þou art swetter þanne mede.
Mankynde! take with þee Bakbytynge!
lefe hym for no maner thynge!
Flepergebet, with hys flaterynge,
standith mankynde in stede.

Detraccion. Bakbytynge & Detraccion
schal goo with þee fro toun to toun.
haue don, Mankynde, & cum doun!
I am þyne owyn page.
I schal bere þee wyttnesse with my myth,
whanne my lord þe Werlde it behyth.
lo, where syr Coueytyse sytt, [Points to his Scaffold on the N.-East.]
& bydith us in his stage.

Humanum Genus. Syr Worlde, I wende, in Coueytyse to chasyn my kende.
Mundus. haue hym in mende! & I-wys þanne schalt þou be ryth þende.

Bonus Angelus. alas, Jhesu, jentyl justyce!
wheder may mans Good Aungyl wende?
now schal careful Coueytyse,
Mankende trewly al [to-]schende;
hys sely goste may sore a-gryse;
Bakbytynge bryngyth hym in bytter bonde.
worldly wyttis, ȝe are not wyse;
ȝour louely lyfe, a-mys ȝe spende,
& þat schal ȝe sore smert.
parkys, poundys, & many pens,
þei semyn to ȝou swetter þanne sens;
but Goddis seruyse, nyn hys commaundementis,
stondyth ȝou not at hert.

Malus Angelus. ȝa! whanne þe fox prechyth, kepe wel ȝore gees!
he speckyth as it were a holy pope.
goo, felaw, & pyke of þe lys
þat crepe þer up-on þi cope!
þi part is pleyed al at þe dys
þat þou schalt haue here, as I hope;
tyl Mankynde fallith to podys prys,
Coueytyse schal hym grype & grope
tyl sum schame hym schende.
tyl man be dyth in dethys dow,
he seyth neuere he hath I-now;
þer-fore, goode boy, cum blow
at my neþer ende!

Detraccio [entering]. Syr Coueytyse, God þee saue,
þi pens & þi poundys all!
I, Bakbytere, þyn owyn knaue,
haue browt Mankynde vn-to þine hall.
þe Worlde bad þou schuldyst hym haue,
& feffyn hym, what-so be-fall.
In grene gres tyl he be graue,
putte hym in þi precyous pall,
Coueytyse! it were all rewthe.
whyl he walkyth in worldly wolde,
I, Bakbyter, am with hym holde;
Lust & Folye, þo barouns bolde,
to hem he hath plyth hys trewthe.

Auaricia [entering]. Ow, Mankynde! blyssyd mote þou be!
I haue louyd þee derworthly many a day,
& so I wot wel þat þou dost me;
cum up & se my ryche a-ray!
it were a gret poynte of pyte
but Coueytyse were to þi pay.
Sit up ryth here in þis se;
I schal þee lere of werldlys lay,
þat fadyth as a flode.
with good I-now I schal þee store;
& ȝyt oure game is but lore,
but þou coueyth mekyl more,
þanne euere schal do þee goode.

þou muste ȝyfe þee to symonye,
extorsion & false asyse;
helpe no man but þou haue why;
pay not þi serwauntys here serwyse!
þi neyborys, loke þou dystroye;
tythe not on non wyse!
here no begger, þou he crye,
& þanne schalt þou ful sone ryse.
& whanne þou vsyste marchaundyse,
loke þat þou be sotel of sleytys,
& also swere al be deseytys,
bye & sell be fals weytys,
for þat is kynde coueytyse.

be not a-gaste of þe grete curse;
þis lofly lyfe may longe leste;
be þe peny in þi purs,
lete hem cursyn, & don here beste.
What, deuyl of hell, art þou þe wers
þow þou brekyste Goddys heste?
Do after me! I am þi nors.
all-wey gadyr, & haue non reste;
in wynnynge be al þi werke!
to pore men take none entent,
for þat þou haste longe tyme hent;
In lytyl tyme it may be spent:
þus seyth Caton, þe grete clerke:
'labitur exiguo quod partum tempore longo.'

Humanum Genus. A, Auaryce! wel þou spede!
of werldly wytte þou canst I-wys;
þou woldyst not I hadde nede,
& schuldyst be wrothe if I ferd a-mys;
I schal neuere begger bede
mete nyn drynke, be heuene blys;
rather or I schulde hym cloþe or fede,
he schulde sterue, & stynke I-wys:
Coueytyse, as þou wylt, I wyl do.
where-so þat I fare, be fenne or flod,
I make a-vow, be Goddys blod,
of Mankynde, getyth no man no good,
but if he synge 'si dedero.'

Auaricia. Mankynde! þat was wel songe:
Sertis now þou canst sum skyll.
blyssyd be þi trewe tonge!
In þis bowre þou schalt byde & byll.
Moo synnys I wolde þou vnderfonge;
with coveytyse þee Feffe I wyll;
& þanne sum Pryde I wolde spronge,
hyȝe in þi hert to holdyn & hyll,
& a-bydyn in þi body.
here I feffe þee in myn heuene
with gold & syluer, lyth as leuene;
þe dedly synnys, alle seuene,
I schal do comyn in hy.

Pryde, Wrathe, & Envye,
Com forthe, þe deuelys chyldryn þre!
Lechery, Slawth, & Glotonye,
to mans flesch ȝe are fendis Fre;
Dryuyth downne ouer dalys drye;
beth now blyþe as any be;
ouer hyll & holtys ȝe ȝou hyȝe,
to com to Mankynde & to me,
fro ȝoure dowty dennys!
as dukys dowty, ȝe ȝou dresse!
whanne ȝe sex be comme, I gesse,
þanne be we seuene, & no lesse,
of þe dedly synnys. [Enter Pride, Wrath and Envy.]

Superbia. Wonder hyȝe howtis, on hyll, herd I houte:
Koueytyse kryeth; hys karpynge I kenne.
Summe lord, or summe lordeyn, lely schal loute
to be pyth with perlys of my proude penne.
bon I am to braggyn, & buskyn a-bowt,
raþely & redyly, on rowte for to renne;
be doun, dalys, nor dennys, no dukis I dowt;
also fast for to Fogge, be flodys & be fenne,
I rore whanne I ryse.
Syr Belyal, bryth of ble!
to ȝou I recomaunde me:
haue good day, my fader fre,
For I goo to Coveytyse.
Ira. Whanne Coveytyse cried, & carpyd of care,
þanne must I, wod wreche, walkyn & wende
hyȝe ouer holtis, as hound aftyr hare.
If I lette, & were þe last, he schuld me sore schende;
I buske my bold baston, be bankis ful bare,
Sum boy schal be betyn, & browth vnder bonde;
Wrath schal hym wrekyn, & weyin his ware;
for-lorn schal al be, for lusti laykys, & londe,
as a lythyr page.
Syr Belyal blak & blo,
haue good day! now I goo
for to fell þi foo
With wyckyd wage.

Invidia. Whanne Wrath gynnyth walke in ony wyde wonys,
Envye flet as a fox, & folwyth on faste.
Whanne þou sterystis or starystis, or stumble up-on stonys,
I lepe as a lyon: me is loth to be þe laste.
ȝa, I breyde bytter balys in body & in bonys;
I frete myn herte, & in kare I me kast.
goo we to Coveytyse, all þre at onys,
with oure grysly gere, a grome for to gast;
þis day schal he deye.
Belsabubbe! now haue good day!
for we wyl wendyn in good a-ray,
al þre in fere, as I þe say,
Pride, Wrath, & Envye.

Belial. Fare-wel now, chyrdryn fayre to fynde!
Do now wel ȝoure olde owse
whanne ȝe com to Mankynde!
make hym wroth & Envyous;
leuyth not lytly vnder lynde:
to his sowle brewyth a bytter jous.
whanne he is ded, I schal hym bynde
In hell, as Catte dothe þe mows:
now buske ȝou forþe on brede!
I may be blythe as any be,
for mankynde, in euery cuntre,
Is rewlyd be my chyldyr þre,
Envye, Wrath, & Pryde. [Exit Belial.]

[Enter Gluttony, Lechery, Sloth and Flesh.]

Gula. a grom gan gredyn gayly on grounde;
of me, gay Glotoun, gan al hys gale.
I stampe & I styrte, & stynt up-on stounde;
to a staunche deth I stakyr & stale.
what boyes, with here belys, in my bondis be bownde,
boþe here bak & here blod, I brewe al to bale;
I fese folke to fyth, tyl here flesch fonde;
Whanne summe han dronkyn a drawth, þei dropyn in a dale;
in me is here mynde.
mans Florchynge flesch,
Fayre, frele & Fresch,
I rape to rewle in a rese,
to kloy et in my kynde.

Luxuria. In mans kyth, I cast me a castel to kepe.
I, Lechery, with lykynge am lovyd in iche a londe.
With my sokelys of swettnesse, I sytte & I slepe;
Many berdys I bryng to my bytter bonde.
In wo & in wrake, wyckyd wytis schal wepe,
þat in my wonys wylde wyl not out wende.
Whanne Mankynde is castyn, undyr clouris to crepe,
þanne þe ledrouns, for here lykynge, I schal al to-schende,
trewly to tell.
Syr Flesch, now I wende,
With lust in my lende,
to cachyn Mankynde
to þe devyl of hell.

Accidia. ȝa! waht seyst þou of Syr Slawth, with my soure syth?
Mankynde louyth me wel wys, as I wene;
men of relygyon, I rewle in my ryth;
I lette Goddis seruyse, þe soþe may be sene.
In bedde I brede brothel, with my berdis bryth;
lordys, ladys, & lederounnys, to my lore leene;
mekyl of mankynde, in my clokis schal be knyth,
tyl deth dryuyth hem down in dalys be-dene:
We may non lenger a-byde.
Syr Flesch, comly kynge,
in þee is al oure bredynge:
ȝeue us now þi blyssynge,
For Coveytyse hath cryde.

Caro. Glotony & slawth, Fare-wel in fere!
louely in londe is now ȝour lesse;
& Lecherye, my Dowter so dere,
Dapyrly ȝe dresse ȝou so dyngne on desse.
All þre, my blyssynge ȝe schal haue here;
goth now forth, & gyue ȝe no fors;
it is no nede, ȝou for to lere
to cachyn Mankynde to a care-ful clos
Fro þe bryth blysse off heuene.
þe Werld, þe Flesch, & þe Devyl, are knowe
grete lordis, as we wel owe,
& þorwe Mankynde we settyn & sowe
þe dedly synnys seuene.
[tunc ibunt Superbia, Ira, Invidia, Gula, Luxuria, & Accidia, ad Auariciam; & dicat Superbia:

Superbia. What is þi wyll, Syr Coveytyse?
Why hast þou afftyr vs sent?
Whanne þou Creydyst, we ganne a-gryse,
& come to þee now par asent;
oure loue is on þee lent.
I, Pryde, Wrath, & Envye,
Gloton, Slawth, & Lechery,
We arn cum all sex for þi Crye,
to be at þi commaundement.
Auaricia. Welcum be ȝe, breþeryn all,
& my sy[s]tyr, swete Lecherye!
wytte ȝe why I gan to call?
for ȝe must me helpe, & þat in hy.
Mankynde is now com to myn hall,
with me to dwell, be downys dry;
þerfore ȝe must, what so be-fall,
Feffyn hym with ȝoure foly,
& ellis ȝe don hym wronge.
For whanne Mankynde is kendly koueytous,
he is provd, wrathful, & Envyous;
Glotons, slaw, & lecherous,
þei arn oþer whyle amonge.

sections.title: Scene VI: The Seven Deadly Sins and the Castle (part 2 of 6)
sections.text:
þus Euery synne tyllyth in oþer,
& makyth Mankynde to ben a foole.
we seuene ffallyn on a fodyr,
Mankynde to chase to pynyngis stole.
þerfore, Pryde, good broþyr,
& breþyryn all, take ȝour tol;
late Iche of vs take at othyr,
& set Mankynde on a stomlynge stol.
whyl he is here on lyve,
lete vs lullyn hym in oure lust,
tyl he be dreuyn to dampnynge dust;
Colde care schal ben hys crust,
to deth whanne he schal dryve.

Superbia. In gle & game I growe glad.
Mankynde, take good hed,
& do as Coveytyse þee bad!
take me in þyn hert, precyous Pryde!
loke þou be not ouer-lad;
late no bacheler þee mysbede;
Do þee to be dowtyd & drad;
bete boyes tyl þey blede;
Kast hem in careful kettis.
Frende, fadyr, & moder dere,
bowe hem not in non manere;
& hold no maner man þi pere,
& vse þese new Iettis:

loke þou blowe mekyl bost,
with longe Crakows on þi schos;
Jagge þi Clothis in euery cost,
& ellis men schul lete þee but a goos.
It is þus, man, wel þou wost;
þerfore do as no man dos,
& euery man sette at a thost,
& of þi-self make gret ros;
now se þi-self on euery syde.
euery man þou schalt schende & schelfe,
& holde no man betyr þanne þi selfe;
tyl dethys dynt þi body delfe,
put holy þyn hert in pryde.

Humanum Genus. Pryde! be Jhesu, þou seyst wel:
Who-so suffyr, is ouer-led al day.
Whyl I reste on my rennynge whel,
I schal not suffre, if þat I may.
Myche myrthe, at mete & mel,
I loue ryth wel, & ryche a-ray.
trewly I þynke, in euery sel,
on grounde to be graythyd gay,
& of my selfe to take good gard.
mykyl myrthe þou wylt me make,
lordlyche to leue, be londe & lake;
myn hert holy to þee I take,
In-to þyn owyn a-ward.

Superbia. I þi bowre to a-byde,
I com to dwelle be þi syde.
Humanum Genus. Mankynde & Pride
schal dwell to-gedyr euery tyde.
Ira. be also wroth, as þou were wode!
Make þee be dred, be dalys derne!
who so þee wrethe, be fen or flode,
loke þou be a-vengyd ȝerne!
be redy to spylle mans blod!
loke þou hem fere, be feldis ferne!
alway, man, be ful of mod!
My lothly lawys, loke þou lerne,
I rede, for any þynge.
a-non take veniaunce, Man, I rede;
& þanne schal no man þee ouer-lede,
but of þee þey schul haue drede,
& bowe to þi byddynge.

Humanum Genus. Wrethe! for þi councel hende,
haue þou Goddis blyssynge & myn!
what caytyf of al my kende
wyl not bowe, he schal a-byn;
with myn veniaunce I schal hym schende,
& wrekyn me, be Goddis yne.
raþer or I schulde bowe or bende,
I schuld be stekyd as a swyne
with a lothly launce.
be it erly or late,
who-so make with me debate,
I schal hym hyttyn on þe pate,
& takyn a-non veniaunce.

Ira. with my rewly rothyr,
I com to þee, Mankynde, my broþer.
Humanum Genus. and Wrethe, þi fayr foþer,
makyth Iche man to be vengyd on oþer.

Invidia. Envye, with Wrathe muste dryve
to haunte Mankynde al-so.
whanne any of þy neyboris wyl þryve,
loke þou haue Envye þer-to.
On þe hey name I charge þee be-lyue,
bakbyte hym, whow-so þou do.
Kyll hym a-non, with-owtyn knyve,
& speke hym sum schame were þou go,
be dale or downys drye.
speke þi neybour mekyl schame;
pot on hem sum fals fame;
loke þou vn-do his nobyl name,
with me, þat am Envye.

Humanum Genus. Envye! þou art boþe good & hende,
& schalt be of my counsel chefe.
þi counsel is knowyn þorwe mankynde,
For ilke man callyth oþer 'hore & thefe.'
Envye, þou arte rote & rynde,
þorwe þis werld, of mykyl myschefe;
In byttyr balys I schal hem bynde,
þat to þee puttyth any reprefe:
cum vp to me above!
for more Envye þanne is now reynynge,
was neuere syth Cryst was kynge.
cum vp, Envye, my dere derlynge!
þou hast Mankyndis love.

Invidia. I clymbe fro þis crofte,
with Mankynde, o, to syttyn on lofte.
Humanum [Genus.] Cum, syt here softe!
For In abbeys þou dwellyst ful ofte.

Gula. In gay glotony, a game þou be-gynne!
ordeyn þee mete & drynkis goode;
loke þat no tresour, þee part a-twynne,
but þee feffe & fede with al kynnys fode.
with fastynge, schal man neuere heuene wynne:
þese grete fasteris, I hold hem wode.
þou þou ete & drynke, it is no synne.
Fast no day, I rede, be þe rode.
þou chyde þese fastyng cherlys!
loke þou haue spycys of goode odoure,
to Feffe & fede þy fleschly floure;
& þanne mayst þou bultyn in þi boure,
& serdyn gay gerlys.

Humanum Genus. A, Glotony! wel I þee grete!
soth & sad it is, þy sawe;
I am no day wel, be sty nor strete,
tyl I haue wel fyllyd my mawe;
fastynge is fellyd vnder Fete.
þou I neuere faste, I rekke [not] an hawe,
he seruyth of nowth, be þe rode, I lete,
but to do a mans gieays to gnawe:
to faste, I wyl not fonde.
I schal not spare, so haue I reste,
to haue a mossel of þe beste:
þe lenger schal my lyfe mow leste,
with gret lykynge in londe.

Gula. Be bankis on brede,
oþerwhyle to spew, þee spede!
Humanum Genus. whyl I lyf lede,
with fayre fode my flesche schal I fede.

Luxuria. ȝa! whanne þi flesche is fayre fed,
þanne schal I, louely Lecherye,
be bobbyd with þee in [þi] bed;
here-of serue mete & drynkis trye.
In loue, þi lyf schal be led;
be a lechour tyl þou dye;
þi nedys schal be þe better sped,
If [þou] ȝyf þee to fleschly folye
tyl deth þee down drepe.
lechery, syn þe werld be-gan,
hath a-vauncyd many a man.
þerfore, Mankynde, my leue lemman,
I my cunte þou schalt crepe.
Humanum Genus. a, lechery, wel þee be!
mans sed in þee is sowe;
fewe men wyl forsake þee,
In any cuntre þat I knowe.
spouse-breche is a frend ryth fre;
men vse þat mo þanne I-nowe;
Lechery, cum syt be me!
þi banys be ful wyd I-knowe;
lykynge is in þi lende.
on, nor oþer, I se no wythte,
þat wyl for-sake [þee] day nor nyth;
þerfore, cum vp, my berd bryth,
& reste þee with Mankynde!

Luxuria. I may soth synge:
'Mankynde is kawt in my slynge.'
Humanum Genus. For ony erthyly þynge,
to bedde þou muste me brynge.

Accidia. ȝa! whanne ȝe be in bedde browth boþe,
wappyd wel in worthy wede,
þanne I, Slawthe, wyl be wrothe,
but ij brothelys I may brede.
whanne þe messe-belle goth,
lye stylle, man, & take non hede!
lappe þyne hed þanne in a cloth,
& take a swet, I þee rede;
Chyrche-goynge þou forsake.
losengeris in londe I lyfte,
& dyth men to mekyl vnthryfte.
Penaunce enjoynyd men in schryfte
is vn-done; & þat I make.

Humanum Genus. Owe, Slawthe, þou seyst me skylle!
men vse þee mekyl, God it wot.
men lofe wel now to lye stylle,
In bedde to take a þorowe swot:
to chyrche-ward, is not here wylle;
here beddys þei þynkyn goode & hot,
Herry, Jofferey, Jone, & Gylle,
arn leyd & logyd in a lot,
with þyne vnþende charmys.
al mankynde, be þe holy rode,
are now slawe in werkis goode.
com nere, þerfore, myn fayre foode,
& lulle me in þyne armys.

Accidia. I make men, I trowe,
In Goddis seruyse to be ryth slowe.
Humanum Genus. Com up þis þrowe!
swyche men þou schalt fynden I-nowe.

Humanum Genus. 'Mankynde' I am callyd be kynde,
with curssydnesse, in costis knet,
In sowre swettenesse my syth I sende,
with seuene synnys sadde be-set.
mekyl myrþe I moue in mynde,
with melody at my mowþis met;
my prowd pouer schal I not pende,
tyl I be putte in peynys pyt,
to helle hent fro hens.
In dale of dole, tyl we are downe,
we schul be clad in a gay gowne:
I se no man but þey vse somme
of þese vij dedly synnys.

for comounly, it is seldom seyne,
who-so now be lecherows,
of oþer men he schal haue dysdeyne,
& ben prowde or Covetous:
In synne iche man is founde.
þer is pore nor ryche, be londe ne lake,
þat alle þese vij wyl forsake,
but with on or oþer he schal be take,
& in here bytter bondis bownde.

Bonus Angelus. So mekyl þe werse, (wele a woo!)
þat euere good aungyl was ordeynyd þee!
þou art rewlyd after þe fende þat is þi foo,
& no þynge, certis, aftyr me.
Weleaway! weder may I goo?
man doth me bleykyn blody ble;
his swete sowle he wyl now sle;
he schal wepe al his game & gle
at on dayes tyme.
ȝe se wel all sothly in syth,
I am a-bowte boþe day & nyth,
to brynge hys sowle in-to blis bryth;
& hym-self wyl it brynge to pyne.

Malus Angelus. No, good aungyl, þou art not in sesun!
ffewe men in þe Feyth þey fynde;
for þou hast schewyd a ballyd resun.
goode syre, cum blowe myn hol be-hynde!
trewly, man hathe non chesun
on þi God to grede & grynde,
For þat schuld cunne Cristis lessoun,
In penaunce, his body he muste bynde,
& forsake þe worldis mende.
men arn loth on þee to crye,
or don penaunce for here folye;
þerfore haue I now maystrye
wel ny ouer al mankynde.

Bonus Angelus. alas! Mankynde
is bobbyt & blent as þe blynde!
In feyth, I fynde,
to Crist he can nowt be kynde.
alas! Mankynne
is soylyd & saggyd in synne!
he wyl not blynne,
tyl body & sowle parte a-twynne.
alas! he is blendyd!
a-mys, mans lyf is I-spendyd,
with fendis fendyd!
mercy, God, þat man were a-mendyd!

Confessio. What! mans aungel, good & trewe!
why syest þou, & sobbyst sore?
sertis, sore it schal me rewe,
If I se þee make mornynge more.
may any bote þi bale brewe,
or any þynge þi stat a-store?
For all felechepys olde & newe,
why makyst þou grochynge vnder gore,
with pynynge poyntis pale?
why was al þis gretynge gunne
with sore syinge vndyr sunne?
tell me, & I schal, if I cunne,
brewe þee bote of bale.

Bonus Angelus. of bytter balys þou mayste me bete,
swete Schryfte, if þat þou wylt.
for Mankynde, it is þat I grete;
he is in poynt to be spylt:
he is set in seuene synnys sete,
& wyl, certis, tyl he be kylt;
with me he þynkyth neuere more to mete
he hath me forsake, & I haue no gylt;
no man wyl hym amende.
þerfore, Schryfte, so God me spede,
but if þou helpe at þis nede,
Mankynde getyth neuere oþer mede,
but peyne with-owtyn ende.
Confescio. what, Aungel! be of comfort stronge,
For þi lordis loue þat deyed on tre!
on me, Schryfte, it schal not be longe,
& þat þou schalt þe sothe se:
if he wyl be a-knowe his wronge,
& no þynge hele, but telle it me,
& don penaunce sone a-monge,
I schal hym stere to gamyn & gle
In joye þat euere schal last.
Who-so schryue hym of his synnys alle,
I be-hete hym heuene halle.
þerfor, go we hens, what so be-falle,
to Mankynde fast.

[tunc ibunt [cum Penitencia] ad humanum genus; & dicat

Confessio. what, Mankynde! whou goth þis?
what dost þou with þese deuelys seuene?
alas, alas! man, al a-mys!
blysse, in þe mane of God in heuene,
I rede, so haue I rest.
þese lotly lordeynys, awey þou lyfte,
& cum doun & speke with Schryfte,
& drawe þee ȝerne to sum thryfte!
trewly it is þe best.

Humanum Genus. a, Schryfte! þou art wel be note
here to Slawthe, þat syttyth here-Inne:
he seyth þou mytyst a com to mannys cote
on Palme-Sunday al be tyme.
þou art com al to sone;
þerfore, Schryfte, be þi fay,
goo forthe tyl on Good Fryday!
tente to þee þanne, wel I may;
I haue now ellys to done.

Confescio. ow! þat harlot is now bold!
In bale he byndyth Mankynde belyue.
Sey, Slawthe, I preyd hym þat he wold
Fynd a charter of þi lyue.
Man! þou mayst ben vndyr mold
longe or þat tyme, kyllyd with a knyue,
with podys & froskis many fold;
þerfore schape þee now to schryue,
if þou wylt com to blys.
þou synnyste, or sorwe þee ensense,
be-hold þynne hert, þi preue spense,
& þynne owyn consyense,
or, sertis, þou dost a-mys.

Humanum Genus. ȝa, Petyr! so do mo!
we haue etyn garlek euerychone.
þou I schulde to helle go,
I wot wel I schal not gon a-lone,
trewly I tell þee.
I dyd neuere so ewyl trewly,
þat oþer han don as ewyl as I.
þerfore, syre, lete be þy cry,
& go hens fro me!

Penitencia. with poynt of penaunce I schal hym preue,
mans pride for to Felle.
with þis launce I schal hym leue,
I-wys, a drope of mercy welle.
Sorwe of hert, is þat I mene:
trewly, þer may no tunge telle,
what waschyth sowlys more clene
ffro þe foul[e] fend of helle,
þanne swete sorwe of hert.
God, þat sytty[t]h in heuene on hye,
askyth no more, or þat þou dye,
but sorwe of hert, with wepynge eye,
for all þi synnys smert.

þei þat syth in synnynge,
In sadde sorwe for here synne,
whanne þei schal make here endynge,
al here joye is to be-gynne.
þanne medelyth no mornynge,
but joye is joynyd with jentyl gynne.
þerfore, Mankynde, in þis tokenynge,
with spete of spere to þee I spynne;
Goddis lawys to þee I lerne.
with my spud of sorwe swote,
I reche to þyne hert[e] rote;
al þi bale schal torne þee to bote:
Mankynde, go schryue þee ȝerne!

Humanum Genus. A sete of sorwe in me is set;
Sertys, for synne I shye sore;
mone of mercy in me is met;
For werldys myrþe I morne more;
In wepynge wo, my wele is wet.
Mercy! þou muste myn fatt a-store;
Fro oure lordys lyth þou hast me let,
sory synne, þou grysly gore!
owte on þee, dedly synne!
synne! þou haste Mankynde schent!
In dedly synne my lyfe is spent.
Mercy! God omnipotent!
In ȝoure grace I be-gynne.

sections.title: Scene VI: The Seven Deadly Sins and the Castle (part 3 of 6)
sections.text:
For þou Mankynde haue don a-mys,
& he wyl falle in repentaunce,
Crist schal hym bryngyn to bowre of blys,
If sorwe of hert lache hym with launce.
lordyngys! ȝe se wel alle, þys,
Mankynde hathe ben in gret bobaunce.
I now for-sake my synne, I-wys,
& take me holy to Penaunce:
on Crist I crye & calle.
a! mercy, Schryfte! I wyl no more;
ffor dedly synne, myn herte is sore;
stuffe Mankynde with þyne store,
& haue hym to þyne halle!
Confescio. Schryffte may no man for-sake.
whanne Mankynde cryeth, I am redy.
whanne sorwe of hert[e] þee hathe take,
Schryfte profytyth veryly.
who-so, for synne, wyl sorwe make,
Crist hym heryth, whanne he wyl criye.
now, Man! lete sorwe þyn synne slake,
& torne not a-geyn to þi Folye,
ffor þat makith dystaunce.
& if it happe þee turne a-geyn to synne,
For Goddis loue, lye not longe þer-Inne!
he þat dothe alway ewyl, & wyl not blynne,
þat askyth gret venjaunce.

Humanum Genus. Nay, sertis, þat schal I not do!
Schryfte! þou schalte þe sothe se;
for þow Mankynde be wonte þer-to,
I wyl now al a-mende me:
I com to þee, Schryfte, al holy, lo! [tunc descendit ad Confessionem.
I forsake ȝou synnys, & fro ȝou fle:
ȝe schapyn to man a sory scho;
whanne he is be-gylyd in þis degre,
ȝe bleykyn al hys ble.
Synne! þou art a sory store!
þou makyst Mankynde to synke sore:
þerfore, of ȝou wyl I no more;
I aske schryfte, for charyte.

Confescio. If þou wylt be a-knowe here
only al þi trespas,
I schal þee schelde fro helle fere,
& putte þee, fro peyne, vn-to precyouse place.
If þou wylt not make þyne sowle clere,
but kepe hem in þynne hert[e] cas,
a-noþer day þey schul be rawe & rere,
& synke þi sowle to Satanas
in gastful glowynge glede.
þerfore, man, in mody monys,
If þou wylt wende to worþi wonys,
schryue þee now, al at onys,
holy of þi mysdede.

Humanum Genus. A, ȝys, Schryfte! trewly I trowe,
I schal not spare, for odde nor even,
þat I schal rekne, al on a rowe,
to lache me up to lyuys leuene;
to my Lord God I am a-knowe,
þat syttyh a-bouen in hey heuene,
þat I haue synnyd many a þrowe
In þe dedly synnys seuene,
boþe in home & halle.
Pride, wrathe, & Envye,
Coueytyse, & lecherye,
slawth, & also glotonye:
I haue hem vsyd alle.

þe x comaundementis, brokyn I haue;
& my fyue wyttis, spent hem a-mys;
I was þanne wood, & gan to raue:
mercy, God! for-geue me þys!
Whanne any pore man gan to me craue,
I gafe hym nowt; & þat forþynkyth me I-wys.
now, seynt Saueour! ȝe me saue,
& brynge me to ȝour boure of blys!
I can not alle say;
but to þe erthe I knele a-down,
boþe with bede & orisoun,
& aske myn absolucioun:
syr Schryfte, I ȝou pray.

Confescio. Now Jhesu Cryste, God holy,—
& all þe seyntis of heuene hende,
Petyr & Powle, apostoly,
to whom God ȝafe powere to lese & bynde,—
he for-ȝeue þee þi foly
þat þou hast synnyd with hert & mynde!
& I, up my powere, þee a-soly,
þat þou hast ben to God vnkynde,
quantum peccasti.
In pride, Ire, & Envye,
slawthe, glotony, & lecherye,
& Coveytyse, continuandelye,
Vitam male continuasti.

I þee a-soyle, with goode entent,
of alle þe synnys þat þou hast wrowth
In brekynge of Goddis commaundement
In worde, werke, wyl & þowth.
I restore to þee [þe] sacrament
Of penauns, weche þou neuere rowt;
þi v. wyttis mys dyspent
In synne, þe weche þou schuldyst nowt,
quicquid gesisti
With eyne sen, herys herynge,
nose smellyd, mowthe spekynge,
& al þi bodys bad werkynge,
Vicium quodcunque fecisti.

I þee a-soyle, with mylde mod,
of al þat þou hast ben ful madde,
In forsakynge of þyn aungyl good,
& þi fowle flesche þat þou hast fadde,
þe werld, þe deuyl þat is so woode,
& folwyd þyne aungyl þat is so badde.
to Jhesu Crist þat deyed on rode,
I restore þee a-geyn ful sadde;
noli peccare!
& all þe goode dedys þat þou haste don,
& all þi tribulacyon,
stonde þee in remyssion:
posius noli viciare.
Humanum Genus. Now, syr Schryfte, where may I dwelle,
to kepe me fro synne & woo?
A comly counseyl ȝe me spelle,
to fende me now fro my foo.
If þese vij synnys here telle
þat I am, þus fro hem goo,
þe werld, þe flesche, & þe deuyl of hell
schul sekyn my soule for to sloo
In-to balys bowre;
þerfore I prey ȝou putte me
In-to sum place of surete,
þat þei may not harmyn me
with no synnys sowre.

Confescio. to swyche a place I schal þee kenne,
þer þou mayst dwelle with-outyn dystaunsce;
& al-wey kepe þee fro synne,
In-to þe Castel of Perseueraunce.
If þou wylt to heuene wynne,
& kepe þee fro werldyly dystaunce,
goo ȝone Castel, & kepe þee þer-Inne,
For [it] is strenger þanne any in Fraunce:
to ȝone castel I þee seende.
þat castel is a precyous place,
ffull of vertu & of grace:
Who-so leuyth þere, his lyuys space,
no synne schal hym schende.

Humanum Genus. a, Schryfte! blessyd mote þou be!
þis castel is here but at honde;
þedyr raþely wyl I tee,
sekyr ouer þis sad sonde.
good perseueraunce, God sende me
whyle I leue here in þis londe!
Fro fowle fylthe now I fle;
Forthe to faryn now I fonde,
to ȝone precyous port.
Lord! what man is in mery lyue
Whanne he is of his synnys schreue!
al my dol a-down is dreue;
Criste is myn counfort.

Malus Angelus. Ey, what deuyl, man! wedyr schat?
woldyst drawe now to holynesse?
goo, felaw, þi goode gate!
þou art forty wynter olde, as I gesse;
goo a-geyn þe deuelys mat,
& pleye þee a whyle with Sare & Sysse!
Sche wolde not ellys, ȝone olde trat,
but putte þee to penaunce & to stresse,
ȝone foule feterel fyle!
late men þat arn on þe pyttis brynke
ffor-beryn boþe mete & drynke,
& do penaunce as hem good þynke,
& cum & pley þee a whyle!

Bonus Angelus. ȝa, Mankynde! wende forthe þi way,
& do no-þynge aftyr hys red!
he wolde þee lede ouer londys lay,
In dale of dros, tyl þou were ded.
of cursydnesse he kepyth þe key,
to bakyn þee a byttyr bred;
In dale of dol tyl þou schudyst dey,
he wolde drawe þee to cursydhed,
In synne to haue myschaunce.
þerfor, spede now þy pace
pertly to ȝone precyouse place
þat is al growyn ful ef grace,
þe Castel of Perseueraunce!

Humanum Genus. goode aungyl, I wyl do as þou wylt,
In londe whyl my lyfe may leste;
ffor I fynde wel in holy wryt,
þou counseylyste euere for þe beste. [He goes up to the Castle.]
Caritas. to charyte, man, haue an eye,
In al þynge, man, I rede.
al þi doynge, as dros is drye,
but in charyte þou dyth þi dede.
I dystroye alwey envye:
so dyd þi God whanne he gan blede;
For synne he was hangyn hye,
& ȝyt synnyd he neuere in dede,
þat mylde mercy welle.
Poule in his pystyl puttyth þe prefe,
'but charyte be with þee chefe,'
þerfore, Mankynde, be now lefe,
In charyte for to dwelle!

Abstiniencia. In abstinens lede þi lyf!
take but skylful refeccyon;
for gloton kyllyth with-owtyn knyf,
& dystroyeth þi complexion.
who-so ete or drynke ouer blyue,
it gaderyth to corrupcion:
þis synne browt us alle in strye,
whanne Adam fel in synne down
fro precyous paradys.
Mankynde! lere now of oure lore!
who-so ete or drynke more,
þanne skylfully hys state a-store,
I holde hym no þynge wys.

Castitas. Mankynde! take kepe of chastyte,
& moue þee to maydyn Marye.
fleschly foly, loke þou fle,
at þe reuerense of oure Ladye.
þat curteys qwene, what dyd sche?
kepte hyr clene & stedfastly,
& in here was trussyd þe trin[i]te;
þorwe gostly grace she was worthy,
& al for sche was chaste.
who-so kepyt hym chast, & wyl not synne,
whanne he is beryed in bankis brynnne,
al hys joye is to be-gynne;
þerfore, to me take taste!

Solicitudo. In besynesse, man, loke þou be,
with worþi werkis goode & þykke!
to slawthe, if þou cast[e] þee,
it schal þee drawe to þowtis wyckke.
Osiositas parit omne malum:
it puttyth a man to pouerte,
& pullyth hym to peynys prycke,
Do sum-what al-wey for loue of me,
þou þou schuldyst but thwyte a stycke;
with bedys, sum tyme þee blys!
Sum tyme rede, & sum tyme wryte,
& sum tyme pleye at þi delyte:
þe deuyl þee waytyth with dyspyte
whanne þou art in Idylnesse.

Largitas. In largyte, man, ley þi loue!
Spende þi good, as God it sent!
In worchep of hym þat syt a-bove,
loke þi goodys be dyspent.
In dale of dros whanne þou schalt droue,
lytyl loue is on þee lent;
þe sekatouris schul seyn it is here be-houe
to make us mery, for he is went,
þat al þis good gan owle.
ley þi tresour & þy trust
In place where no ruggynge rust
may it dystroy to dros ne dust,
but al to helpe of sowle.

Humanum Genus. ladys in lond, louely & lyt,
lykynge lelys, ȝe be my leche!
I wyl bowe to ȝour byddynge bryth;
trewe tokenynge ȝe me teche.
dame Meknes, in ȝour myth,
I wyl me wryen ffro wyckyd wreche;
al my purpos I haue pyt,
paciens to don, as ȝe me preche;
fro wrathe ȝe schal me kepe.
Charyte! ȝe wyl to me entende;
fro fowle Envye ȝe me defende!
manis mende ȝe may a-mende,
whether he wake or slepe.

Abstynens, to ȝou I tryst;
fro Glotony ȝe schal me drawe;
In chastyte, to leuyn me lyst,
þat is oure ladys lawe.
Besynes, we schul be cyste;
Slawthe, I forsake þi sleper sawe;
Largyte, to ȝou I tryst,
Coveytyse to don of dawe:
þis is a curteys cumpany.
what schuld I more monys make?
þe seuene synnys I forsake,
& to þese vij vertuis I me tak.
Maydyn Meknes, now, mercy!

Humilitas. Mercy may mende al þi mone:
Cum in here at þynne owyn wylle! [Mankind goes into the Castle.]
we schul þee fende fro þi fon Cum sancto sanctus eris, & cetera.
if þou kepe þee in þis castel stylle;
stonde here-Inne, as stylle as ston;
þanne schal no dedly synne þee spylle:
wheþer þat synnys cumme or gon,
þou schalt with us þi bouris bylle;
with vertuse we schul þee vaunce.
þis Castel is of so qweynt a gynne,
þat who-so-euere holde hym þer-Inne,
he schal neuere fallyn in dedly synne:
it is þe Castel of Perseueranse.
Qui perseuerauerit usque in finem, hic saluus erit.
[Tunc cantabunt 'eterne rex altissime, &[c].'

Humilita[s]. now, blyssyd be oure Lady, of heuene Emperes!
now is Mankynde fro foly falle,
& is in þe Castel of Goodnesse.
he hauntyth now heuene halle
þat schal bryngyn hym to heuene.
Crist þat dyed, with dyen dos,
kepe Mankynde in þis Castel clos,
& put alwey in his purpos
to fle þe synnys seuene!

Malus Angelus. Nay! be Belyals bryth bonys,
þer schal he no whyle dwelle.
he schal be wonne fro þese wonys,
with þe Werld, þe Flesch, & þe Deuyl of hell;
þei schul my wyl a-wreke.
þe synnys seuene, þe kyngis thre,
to Mankynde haue enmyte;
scharpely þei schul helpyn me,
þis Castel for to breke.

Howe! Flypyrgebet! Bakbytere!
ȝerne, oure message, loke þou make!
blythe a-bowt loke þou bere!
sey, Mankynde his synnys hath for-sake;
with ȝene wenchys he wyl hym were.
al to holynesse he hath hym take;
In myn hert it doth me dere;
þe bost þat þo moderis crake,
My galle gynnyth to grynde.
Flepyrgebet! ronne up-on a rasche!
byd þe Werld, þe Fend, & þe Flesche,
þat þey com to fytyn fresche,
to wynne a-ȝeyn Mankynde.
Detraccio. I go, I go, on grounde glad,
swyfter þanne schyp with rodyr!
I make men masyd & mad,
& euery man to kyllyn odyr
with a sory chere.
I am glad, be Seynt Jamys of Galys,
Of schrewdnes to tellyn talys
boþyn in Ingelond & in Walys,
& feyth I haue many a fere. [tunc ibu[nt] ad Belial.

heyl, set in þyn selle!
heyl, dynge deuyl in þi delle!
heyl, lowe in helle!
I cum to þee, talys to telle.

Belyal. Bakbyter, boy! alwey be holtis & hethe,
Sey now, I sey, what tydyngis? telle me þe sothe!

Detraccio. teneful talys I may þee sey;
to þee no good, as I gesse:
Mankynde is gon now a-wey
In-to þe Castel of Goodnesse;
þer he wyl boþe lyuyn & deye,
In dale of dros tyl deth hym dresse:
hathe þee forsakyn, forsoþe I sey,
& all þi werkis, more & lesse;
to ȝone Castel he gan to crepe.
ȝone modyr Meknes, sothe to sayn,
& all ȝene maydnys on ȝone playn,
for to fytyn þei be ful fayn,
Mankynde for to kepe.
[tunc vertunt Superbia, Inuidia, & Ira.

Superbia. Syr kynge, what wytte?
We be redy, protis to kytte.
Belyal. Sey, gadelyngis! haue ȝe harde grace!
& euyl deth mote ȝe deye!
why lete ȝe Mankynde fro ȝou pase
In-to ȝene Castel, fro us a-weye?
with tene I schal ȝou tey.
harlotis! at onys
fro þis wonys!
be Belyals bonys,
ȝe schul a-beye! [& verberabit eos super terram.

Detraccio. ȝa! for God, þis was wel goo,
þus to werke with Bakbytynge!
I werke boþe wrake & woo,
& make Iche man, oþer to dynge.
I schal goo a-bowte, & makyn moo
rappys for to route & rynge.
ȝe bakbyteris, loke þat ȝe do so!
make debate abowtyn to sprynge
be-twene syster & broþer!
if any bakbyter here be lafte,
he may lere of me hys crafte;
of Goddis grace he schal be rafte,
& euery man to kyllyn oþer. [ad Carnem.

heyle, kynge I-calle!
heyl, prinse, proude prekyd in palle!
heyl, hende in halle!
heyl, syr kynge! fayre þee be-falle!

sections.title: Scene VI: The Seven Deadly Sins and the Castle (part 4 of 6)
sections.text:
Caro. Roy Bakbytynge,
ful redy in robys to rynge!
ful glad tydynge,
be Belyalys bonys, I trow þow brynge.

Detraccio. ȝa, for God, owt I crye
on þi too sonys & þi dowtyr ȝynge:
Glotoun, Slawthe, & Lechery,
hath put me in gret mornynge.
þey let Mankynde gon up hye
In-to ȝene castel at hys lykynge,
þer-in for to leue & dye,
with þo ladys to make endynge,
þe flouris fayre & fresche.
he is in þe Castel of Perseuerauns,
& put hys body to penauns;
of hard happe is now þi chauns,
Syr kynge, Mankyndys flesche. [tunc Caro clamabit ad Gulam, Accidiam, & Luxuriam.

Luxuria. Sey now þi wylle!
Syr Flesch, why cryest þou so schylle?

Caro. A, Leechery, þou skallyd mare!
& þou Gloton, God ȝeue þee wo!
& vyle Slawth, euyl mote þou fare!
Why lete ȝe Mankynde fro ȝou go
In ȝone Castel so hye?
euele grace com on þi snowte!
now I am dressyd in gret dowte.
Why nad ȝe lokyd betyr a-bowte?
be Belyalys bonys, ȝe shul a-bye! [tunc uerberant eos in placeam.

Detraccio. Now, be God, þis is good game!
I, Bakbyter, now bere me wel.
if I had lost my name,
I vow to God it were gret del.
I schape þese schrewys to mekyl schame:
iche rappyth on oþer with rowtynge rele;
I, Bakbyter, with fals fame
Do brekyn & brestyn hodys of stele;
þorwe þis cuntre I am knowe.
now wyl I gynne forth to goo,
& make Coueytyse haue a knoke or too;
& þanne I-wys I haue doo
my deuer, as I trowe. [ad Mundum.

heyl, styf in stounde!
heyl, gayly gyrt up on grounde!
heyl, fayre flowr I founde!
heyl, syr Werld, worþi in wodis wonde!

Mundus. Bakbyter in rowte!
þou tellyst talys of dowte,
So styf & so stowte.
what tydyngis bryngyst þou a-bowte?

Detraccio. No-þynge goode: þat schalt þou wete.
Mankynde, syr Werld, hath þee for-sake;
with Schryfte & Penauns he is smete,
& to ȝene Castel he hath hym take,
a-monge ȝene ladys, whyt as lak[e].
lo, syr Werld! ȝe mown a-gryse
þat ȝe be seruyd on þis wyse.
go pley ȝou with syr Coueytyse
tyl his crowne crake! [tunc buccinabunt cornuo ad Auariciam.

Auaricia (entering). Syr bolnynge bowde,
tell me why blowe ȝe so lowde!

Mundus. lowde losel! þe deuel þee brenne!
I prey God ȝeue þee a fowl hap!
sey, why letyst þou Mankynde
In-to ȝene castel for to skape!
I trow þou gynnyst to raue.
now, for Mankynde is went,
al oure game is schent:
þerfore, a sore dryuynge dent,
harlot, þou shalt haue! [tunc uerberant eum.

Auaricia. Mercy! mercy! I wyl no more;
þou hast me rappyd with rewly rowtis!
I snowre, I sobbe, I sye sore!
myn hed is clateryd al to clowtis!
In al ȝoure state I schal ȝou store,
if ȝe abate ȝoure dyntis dowtis.
Mankynde, þat ȝe haue for-lore,
I schal do com owt fro ȝone skowtis
to ȝoure hende hall.
if ȝe wyl no more betyn me,
I schal do Mankynde com out fre;
he schal for-sake, as þou schalt se,
þe fayre vertus all.

Mundus. Haue do þanne! þe deuyl þee tere!
þou schalt ben hangyn in hell herne.
by-lyue, my baner up þou bere,
& be-sege we þe castel ȝerne,
Mankynde for to stele.
whanne Mankynde growyth good,
I, þe Werld, am wylde & wod;
þo bycchys schul bleryn in here blood,
with Flappys felle & fele.

ȝerne lete flapyr up my fane,
& schape we schance & schonde!
I schal brynge with me þo bycchys bane;
þer schal no vertus dwellyn in my londe.
Mekenes is þat modyr þat I mene:
to hyre I brewe a bytter bonde;
Sche schal dey up-on þis grene,
if þat sche com al in myn honde,
ȝeue rappokis with here rumpys.
I am þe Werld! it is my wyll,
þe Castel of Vertu for to spyll.
Howtyth hye up-on ȝene hyll,
ȝe traytours in ȝoure trumpys! [tunc Mundus, Cupiditas, & Stulticia ibunt ad castellum cum vexillo & domino Demon.

Belyal. I here trumpys trebelen al of tene
þe worþi Werld walkyth to werre,
for to clyuyn ȝone Castel clene,
þe maydnys meyndys for to merre.
sprede my penon up on a prene,
& stryke we forthe now vndyr sterre!
schapyth now ȝoure scheldys schene,
ȝene skallyd skoutis for to skerre
up-on ȝone grene grese!
buske ȝou now, boyes, be-lyue! tunc mutabit.
for euere I stonde in mekyl stryue;
whyl Mankynde is in clene lyue,
I am neuere wel at ese.

make ȝou redy, alle þre,
bolde battyl for to bede!
to ȝone feld[e] lete us fle,
& bere my baner forthe on brede!
to ȝone castel wyl I te;
þo mameryng modrys schul haue here mede.
but þei ȝeld[yn] up to me,
with byttyr balys þei schul blede;
of here reste I schal hem reue.
In woful watrys I schal hem wasche.
haue don, felaus! & take ȝoure trasche,
& wende we þedyr on a rasche,
þat castel for to cleue.

Superbia. Now, now! now, go now!
on hye hyllys lete us howte—
for in pride is al my prow—
þi bolde baner to bere a-bowte.
to Golyas I make a vow
for to schetyn ȝone Iche skowte.
on hyr ars, raggyd & row,
I schal boþe clatyr & clowte,
& ȝeue Meknesse myschanse.
Belyal bryth! it is þyn hest
þat I, Pryde, goo þee nest,
& bere þi baner beforn my brest
with a comly contenaunce.

Caro. I here an hydowse whwtynge on hyt:
be-lyue byd my baner forth for to blase!
wahanne I syt in my sadyl, it is a selkowth syt;
I gape as a Gogmagog whanne I gynne to gase:
þis worthy, wylde werld, I wagge with a wyt;
ȝone rappokis I ruble, & al to-rase;
boþe with schot & with slynge I caste with a sleyt,
with care to ȝone castel to crachen & to crase
In Flode.
I am mans flesch: where I go
I am mans most fo;
I-wys I am euere wo
whane he drawyth to goode.

þerfor, ȝe bolde boyes, buske ȝou a-bowte!
scharply on scheldis, ȝour schaftys ȝe scheuere!
& Lechery ledron, schete þou a skoute!
help we, Mankynde fro ȝone castel to keuere!
helpe! we mon hym wynne.
schete we all at a schote,
with gere þat we cunne best note,
to chache Mankynde fro ȝene cote
In-to dedly synne.

Gula. Lo, syr Flesch, whov I fare to þe felde,
with a faget on myn hond, for to settyn on a fyre!
with a wrethe of þe wode, wel I can me welde;
with a longe launce, þe loselys I schal lere.
go we with oure gere!
þe bycchys schul bleykyn & blodyr,
I schal makyn swyche a powdyr,
boþe with smoke & with somodyr,
þei schul schytyn for fere. [tunc descendunt in placea.

Malus Angelus. 'as armys,' as an heyward, hey now I howte.
Deuyl dyth þee as a duke, to do þe damyselys dote! [dicat ad Belyal.
Belyal, as a bolde boy, þi brodde I bere a-bowte:
helpe to cache Mankynde fro caytyfys cote!
Pryd! put out þi penon of raggys & of rowte!
Do þis modyr Mekenes meltyn to mote!
Wrethe! prefe Paciens, þe skallyd skowte!
Envye, to Charyte, schape þou a schote
Ful ȝare!
With Pryde, Wrethe & Envye,
þese deuelys, be downys drye,
as comly kynge, I dyscrye,
Mankynde to kachyn to care. [ad Carnem.

Flesch, frele & fresche, frely fed!
with Gloton, Slawthe & Lechery, mans sowle þou slo!
as a duke dowty, do þee to be dred;
gere þee with geris fro toppe to þe too!
kyth þis day þou art a kynge frely fedde! [to Glutton]
Gloton! sle þou Abstyne[n]sce with wyckyd woo!
with Chastyte, þou Lechour, be not ouyr-ledde!
Slawthe! bete þou Besynes on buttokys bloo!
do now þi crafte, in coste to be knowe! [ad Mundum.
worthy, wytty, & wys, wondyn in wede!
lete Coueytyse karpyn, cryen & grede!
here ben bolde bacheleris, batyl to bede,
Mankynde to tene, as I trowe.
Humanum Genus. þat dynge duke þat deyed on rode,
þis day, my sowle kepe & safe!
whanne Mankynde drawyth to goode,
be-holde what enmys he schal haue!
þe Werld, þe Deuyl, þe Flesche, arn wode;
to men ben casten a careful kaue;
byttyr balys þei brekyn on brode,
Mankynde in wo to weltyr & waue,
lordyngis, sothe to sey.
þerfore Iche man be-war of þis!
for, whyl Mankynde clene is,
his enmys schul temptyn hym to don a-mys,
if þei mown, be any wey.

Omne gaudium existimate, cum variis temtacionibus insideritis.
þerfor, lordys, beth now glad,
with elmes dede & orysoun
for to don as oure Lord bad!
styfly with-stonde ȝoure temptacyoun!
with þis foul fende I am ner mad.
to batayle þei buskyn hem bown.
certis, I schuld ben ouer-lad,—
but þat I am in þis castel town,—
with synnys sore & smerte.
who so wyl leuyn oute of dystresse,
& ledyn hys lyf in clennesse,
In þis castel of vertu & of goodnesse
hym muste haue hole his hert.
delectari in domino, & dabit tibi peticiones cordis tui.

Bonus Angelus. A! Mekenesse, Charyte & Pacyens,—
prymrose pleyeth parlasent,—
Chastyte, Besynes, & Abstynens,
myn hope, ladys, in ȝou is lent!
so come paramourys, swetter þanne sens,
Rode as rose on rys I-rent!
þis day ȝe dyth a good defens!
whyl Mankynde is in good entent,
his þoutis arn vn-hende.
Mankynde is browt in-to þis walle,
In freelte to fadyn & falle;
þerfore, ladys, I pray ȝou alle,
helpe þis day Mankynde!

Humilitas. God, þat syttyth in heuene on hy,
saue al Mankynde be se & sonde!
lete hym dwellyn here, & ben vs by,
& we schul puttyn to hym helpynge honde.
ȝyt forsoþe neuere I sy
þat any fawte in vs he fonde,
but þat we sauyd hym fro synne sly,
if he wolde be us styfly stonde
In þis castel of ston.
þerfor drede þee not, mans aungel dere!
if he wyl dwellyn with vs here,
Fro seuene synnys we schul hym were,
& his enmys Ichon.

now, my seuene systerys swete, [To the Seven Virtues.]
þis day fallyth on us þe lot,
Mankynde for to schylde & schete
fro dedly synne & schamely schot.
hys enmys strayen in þe strete,
to spylle man with spetows spot;
þerfor oure flouris, lete now flete,
& kepe we hym, as we haue het,
amonge vs in þis halle.
þerfor, vij systeris swote,
lete oure vertus reyne on rote!
þis day we wyl be mans bote
a-geyns þese deuelys alle.

Belyal. þis day, þe vaward wyl I holde.
a-vaunt my baner, precyous Pride,
Mankynde to cache to karis colde!
bold batayl now wyl I byde.
buske ȝou, boyes, on brede!
alle men þat be with me wytholde,
boþe þe ȝonge & þe olde,
Envye, Wrathe, ȝe boyes bolde,
to rounde rappys ȝe rape, I rede!

Superbia. As armys, Mekenes! I brynge þi bane,
al with pride, peyntyd & pyth.
what seyst þou, faytour? be myn fayr fane,
with robys rounde, rayed ful ryth,
grete gounse, I schal þee gane!
to marre þee, Mekenes, with my myth.
no werldly wyttys here ar wane;
lo! þi castel is al be-set!
moderis! whov schul ȝe do?
Mekenes! ȝelde þee to me, I rede.
myn name in londe is precyous Prede;
myn bolde baner to þee I bede:
modyr! what seyste þer-to?

Humilitas. a-geyns þi baner of pride & bost,
a baner of meknes & mercy
I putte ageyns pride, wel þou wost,
þat schal schende þi careful cry.
þis meke Kyng is knowyn in euery cost,
þat was croysyd on Caluary.
whanne he cam down fro heuene ost,
& lytyd with mekenes in Mary,
þis Lord þus lytyd lowe.
whanne he cam fro þe Trynyte,
In-to a maydyn lytyd he,
& al was for to dystroye þee:
Pride, þis schalt þou knowe.
Deposuit potentes de sede, & cetera.
for, whanne Lucyfer to helle fyl,
Pride, þer-of þou were chesun;
& þou, deuyl, with wyckyd wyl,
In paradys trappyd us with tresun,
so þou us bond in balys Ille:
þis may I preue be ryth resun.
tyl þis Duke þat dyed on hylle,
in heuene man myth neuere han sesun;
þe gospel þus declaryt.
for who-so lowe hym, schal ben hy;
þerfore þou schalt not comen us ny;
& þou þou be neuere so sly,
I schal felle al þi fare.
qui se exaltat, humiliabitur, & cetera.

Ira. Dame Pacyens! what seyst þou to Wrathe & Ire?
putte Mankynde fro þi castel clere,
or I schal tappyn at þi tyre
with styffe stonys þat I haue here.
I schal slynge at þee many a vyre,
& ben a-vengyd hastely here:
þus Belsabub, oure gret syre,
bad me brenne þee with wyld fere,
þou bycche blak as kole.
þerfor, fast, fowle skowte,
putte Mankynde to us owte,
or of me þou schalt haue dowte,
þou modyr, þou motyhole!

Paciencia. fro þi dowte, Crist me schelde
þis Iche day, & al mankynde!
þou wrecchyd wreche, wood & wylde,
Pacyens schal þee schende!
quia ira viri, justicia Dei non operatur.
for Marys sone, meke & mylde,
rent þee up, rote & rynde,
whanne he stod meker þanne a chylde,
& lete boyes hym betyn & bynde:
þerfor, wrecche, be stylle!
for þo pelouris þat gan hym pose,
he myth a dreuyn hem to dros;
& ȝyt, to casten hym on þe cros,
he sufferyd al here wylle.

þowsentis of aungellis he myth han had,
to a wrokyn hym þer ful ȝerne;
& ȝyt, to deyen he was glad,
us, pacyens to techyn & lerne.
þerfor, boy, with þi boystous blad,
fare a-wey be feldys ferne!
for I wyl do as Jhesu bad,
wrecchys, fro my wonys werne
with a dyngne defens.
if þou fonde to comyn a-lofte,
I schal þee cache fro þis crofte
with þese rolys swete & softe,
peyntyd with pacyens.

Inuidia. Out! myn herte gynnyth to breke,
for Charyte þat stondyth so stowte.
alas! myn herte gynnyth to wreke.
ȝelde up þis castel, þou hore clowte!
it is myn offyce, fowle to speke,
fals sklaundrys to bere a-bowte.
Charyte! þe deuyl mote þee cheke,
but I þee rappe with rewly rowte,
þi targe for to tere.
let Mankynde cum to us doun,
or I schal schetyn to þis castel town
a ful fowle defamacyoun;
þerfore þis bowe I bere.
Caritas. þou þou speke wycke & fals[e] fame,
þe wers schal I neuere do my dede.
who-so peyryth falsly a-noþer mans name,
Cristys curs he schal haue to mede:
ve homini illi per quem scandalum ven[it].
who-so wyl not hys tunge tame,—
take it sothe, as mes crede,—
wo, wo, to hym, & mekyl schame!
In holy wrytte þis I rede;
for euere þou art a schrewe.
þou þou speke euyl, I ne ȝeue a gres;
I schal do neuere þe wers;
At þe last, þe sothe vers
certis hym-self schal schewe.

sections.title: Scene VI: The Seven Deadly Sins and the Castle (part 5 of 6)
sections.text:
Oure louely Lord, with-owtyn lak,
ȝaf example to charyte:
whanne he was betyn blo & blak
for trespas þat neuere dyd he,—
In sory synne had he no tak,
& ȝyt for synne he bled blody ble,—
he toke his cros up on his bak,
synful man, & al for þee:
þus he mad defens.
Envye, with þi slaundrys þycke,
I am putte at my Lordys prycke;
I wyl do good a-ȝeyns þe wycke,
& kepe in sylens.

Belyal. What, for Belyalys bonys,
where a-bowtyn chyde ȝe?
haue don, ȝe boyes, al at onys!
lasche don þese moderys, alle þre!
werke wrake to þis wonys!
þe vaunward is grauntyd me.
do þese moderys to makyn monys!
ȝoure dowty dedys, now lete se!
dasche hem al to daggys!
haue do, boyes blo & blake!
wirke þese wenchys wo & wrake!
Claryouns, cryith up at a krake,
& blowe ȝour brode baggys! [tunc pugnabunt domini.

Superbia. Out! my prowde bak is bent!
Mekenes hath me al for-bete;
Pride with Mekenes is for-schent.
I weyle & wepe, with wondys wete;
I am betyn in þe hed.
my prowde pride a-doun is dreuyn,
so scharpely Mekenes hath me schreuyn,
þat I may no lenger leuyn;
my lyf is me be-reuyd.

Invidia. Al myn Enmyte is not worth a fart;
I schyte & schake al in my schete;
Charyte, þat sowre swart,
with fayre rosys myn hed gan breke:
I brede þe malaundyr.
with worthi wordis & flouris swete,
Charyte makyth me so meke,
I dare neyþer crye nore crepe,
not a schote of sklaundyr.

Ira. I, Wrethe, may syngyn wele-a-wo.
Pacyens me ȝaf a sory dynt;
I am al betyn blak & blo
with a rose þat on rode was rent;
my speche is almost spent.
hyr rosys fel on me so scharpe,
þat myn hed hangyth as an harpe:
I dar neyþer crye nor carpe;
sche is so pacyent.
Malus Angelus. go hens! ȝe do not worthe a tord!
foule falle ȝou, alle foure!
ȝerne, ȝerne, let fall on bord!
Syr Flesch, with þyn ey[e]n soure,
for care I cukke & koure.
syr Flesch, with þyn company,
ȝerne, ȝerne, make a crye!
helpe we haue no velony,
þat þis day may be oure!

Caro. war, war! late mans flesche go to!
I com with a company.
haue do, my chyldryn! now haue do,
Gloton, Slawth, & Lechery!
Iche of ȝou wynnyth a scho.
lete not Mankynde with maystry!
lete slynge hem in a fowl[e] slo,
& fonde to feffe hym with foly!
dothe now wel ȝoure dede!
ȝerne lete se whov ȝe schul gynne,
Mankynde to temptyn to dedly synne.
if ȝe muste þis castele wynne,
hell schal be ȝour mede.

Gula. war! syr Gloton schal makyn a smeke
a-ȝeyns þis castel, I vowe.
Abstynens! þou þou bleyke,
I loke on þee with bytter browe.
I haue a faget in myn necke,
to settyn Mankynde on a lowe;
my foul leye schalt þou not let,
I wou to God, as I trowe;
þerfor putte hym out here!
In meselynge glotonye,
with goode metis & drynkys trye,
I norche my syster Lecherye
tyl man rennyth on fere.
Abstinencia. þi metis & drynkys arn vnthende:
whanne þei are out of mesure take,
þei makyn men mad & out of mende,
& werkyn hem bothe wo & wrake.
þat, for þi fere þou þou here kyndyl,
certis I schal þi wele a-slake
with bred þat browth us out of hell,
& on þe croys sufferyd wrake:
I mene þe sacrament;
þat Iche blysful bred
þat hounge on hyl tyl he was ded,
schal tempere so myn maydynhed,
þat þi purpos schal be spent.

In abstynens þis bred was browth,
certys, Mankynde, & al for þee.
of fourty dayes ete he nowth,
& þanne was naylyd to a tre;
example us was be-tawth:
In sobyrnesse he bad us be.
þerfor Mankynde schal not be cawth,
Glotony, with þy degre:
þe sothe þou schalt se.
to norysch fayre, þou þou be fawe,
abstynens, it schal with-drawe
tyl þou be schet vnder schawe,
& fayn for to fle.

Luxuria. lo, Chastyte, þou fowle skowte!
þis ilke day here þou schalt deye.
I make a fer in mans towte,
þat launcyth up as any leye.
þese cursyd colys I bere abowte,
Mankynde in tene for to teye.
men & wommen hathe no dowte,
with pyssynge pokys for to pleye;
I bynde hem in my bondys.
I haue no reste, so I rowe,
with men & wommen, as I trowe,
tyl I, Lechery, be set on a lowe,
In al Mankyndis londys.

Casti[t]as. I, Chastyte, haue power in þis place,
þee, Lechery, to bynd & bete.
Madyn Marye, well of grace,
schal qwenche þat fowle hete.
oure Lord God mad þee no space
whanne his blod strayed in þe strete.
fro þis castel he dyd þee chase
whanne he was crounyd with þornys grete
& grene.
to drery deth whanne he was dyth,
& boyes dyd hym gret dyspyth,
In lechery had he no delyth,
& þat was ryth wel sene.

at oure Lady I lere my iessun,
to haue chaste lyf tyl I be ded.
sche is qwene, & beryth þe croun;
& al was for hyr maydynhed.
þerfor go fro þis castel toun,
Lechery, now I þee rede;
for Mankynde getyst þou nowth doun,
to sowen hym synful sede:
In care þou woldys hym cast.
& if þou com up to me,
trewly þou schalt betyn be
with þe ȝerde of Chastyte
whyl my lyf may last.

Accidia. Ware, war! I delue with a spade;
men calle me þe 'lord syr Slowe.'
gostly grace I spylle & schade;
fro þe watyr of grace, þe dyche I fowe;
ȝe schulyn com ryth I-nowe
be þis dyche drye, be bankys brede.
xxxti thousende þat I wel knowe,
In my lyf louely I lede,
þat had leuere syttyn at þe ale,
iij mens songys to syngyn lowde,
þanne to-ward þe chyrche for to crowde.
þou Besynesse, þou bolnyd bowde!
I brewe to þee þyne bale.

Solicitudo. a, good men! be-war now all
of Slugge & Slawthe, þe fowl[e] þefe!
to þe sowle he is byttyrer þanne gall;
rote he is of mekyl myschefe;
Goddys seruyse, þat ledyth us to heuene hall,
þis lordeyn, for to lettyn us, is lefe.
who-so wyl schryuyn hym of his synnys all,
he puttyth þis brethel to mykyl myschefe,
Mankynde, he þat myskaryed.
men moun don no penauns for hym þis,
nere schryue hem whanne þey don a-mys,
but euer he wold, in synne I-wys,
þat Mankynde were taryed.

þerfor he makyth þis dyke drye,
to puttyn Mankynde to dystresse;
he makyth dedly synne a redy weye
In-to þe Castel of Goodnesse;
but with tene I schal hym teye,
þorwe þe helpe of heuene emperesse;
with my bedys he schal a-beye;
& oþer ocupacyons more & lesse
I schal schape, hym to schonde,
for whoso wyle Slawth putte doun
with bedys & with orysoun
or sum oneste ocupacyoun,
as boke to haue in honde.
